title: Computer Use
intro: Let DSH operate Windows desktop apps and web pages.
indicatorHint: Lights a screen border glow and banner during control; hides after 30 idle seconds.
delayHint: How long the indicator stays after an action: 200–3000 ms.
stopHint: Esc stops this round at once; the next task works normally. Use DSH stop button for background web tasks.
unavailable: Writable settings are unavailable. Open this page in your local DSH host.
invalid: Use 1–120 characters on one line and an integer hide delay between 200 and 3000.
persistFailed: The host did not confirm the saved settings. Refresh and retry.

issueBefore: Found a problem or have a wish?
issueAfter: — you make the wish, I’ll work on it!
shortcutHint: Add an extra stop key: click Record shortcut, press a key, then save. Esc always works.
unsupportedKey: Use a letter, number, function key or common key, optionally with Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win.
recordUnavailable: Could not pause desktop shortcuts. Start recording again.
recordTimedOut: Recording timed out. Click the button to try again.

toolHint_snapshot: Capture the screen and UI controls
toolHint_find: Find controls by text or type
toolHint_click: Click a control or screen position
toolHint_move: Move the pointer to a position
toolHint_type_text: Enter text at the current focus
toolHint_keypress: Send a key or key combination
toolHint_launch_app: Start an app that remains open after the tool exits
toolHint_activate_window: Bring a window to the foreground
toolHint_close_window: Ask an app to close a window
toolHint_focus: Move input focus to a control
toolHint_invoke: Invoke, toggle, select or expand a control
toolHint_batch: Run planned actions in order and stop on changes
toolHint_wait_for: Wait for a window, control or text
customSummary: Choose exactly which tools to load
lazySummary: Start with management only; load desktop tools on demand
remoteVisible: Visible in remote sessions and recordings
remoteVisibleHint: Allow recordings, screen sharing, and remote sessions to capture overlays (including displayed reasoning).
pluginDescription: Let the agent use Windows apps and web pages, with Browser Use, control indicators, stop shortcuts and tool selection.
notLoaded: Computer Use settings could not be read. The host has not exposed this configuration. Refresh or restart DSH.
browserAttachUserHint: Control your active Chrome or Edge with existing sign-ins. Prompts Allow before each connection.
attachStep1: Open the address below in your browser and enable “Allow remote debugging for this browser instance”.
attachStep2: Click Allow in the browser when DSH asks to connect. Refusals or timeouts are not retried automatically.
attachRisk1: DSH acts as you on every signed-in site here. Told to ask before sending, paying, or deleting, though not guaranteed.
attachRisk2: Malicious pages can try to mislead DSH. While remote debugging stays on, other local apps can also request browser control.
progressOverlayHint: Shows DSH current step and reasoning in a screen corner. Translucent, click-through, stays 20s after a turn.
progressLockedHint: When locked, clicks pass right through. Hover the top-right padlock icon briefly to move or resize.
progressShortcutHint: Press or type a shortcut (e.g. Ctrl+Alt+P) to toggle lock; leave empty for none.
progressSync: Drag or resize auto-saves; click × when done.
progressModeHint: Source shows full DSH reasoning. AI summary condenses it to one or two lines using a few extra tokens.
browserInfo: DSH starts a clean browser without your sign-ins or history. You can keep sign-ins or attach to your active browser.
browserAppHint: Pick the DSH browser. Default follows your system browser, or falls back to Chrome or Edge.
firefoxNotice: Firefox support is experimental and runs headless without manual sign-in. Choose Chrome or Edge for a visible window.
browserSignInHint: Keep website sign-ins across tasks in the DSH browser, separate from your personal browser.
signInStep1: Sign in once inside the blue-framed DSH browser window to stay logged in; your personal browser stays untouched.
signInStep2: When a site asks to log in, DSH pauses for you to enter passwords and codes yourself.
signInStepHidden: The DSH browser window is hidden: turn on “Show the DSH browser window” to sign in first, then turn it back off if you prefer.
signInStepEdge: Edge signs in automatically with your Windows Microsoft account (Bing, Outlook…). Choose Chrome to avoid this.
signInStep3: Sign-ins remain in the folder below even if switched off. To wipe them, exit DSH and delete that folder.
signInRisk1: DSH acts as you on signed-in sites (messaging, orders, deletions); told to ask first, though not guaranteed.
signInRisk2: Malicious page content can try to steer DSH into unintended actions.
signInRisk3: Sign-ins live in a local profile folder that other programs under your Windows account can also read.
browserFirstHint: Prefer fast background page controls without moving your pointer; falls back seamlessly when turned off.
browserVisibleHint: Show the DSH browser window on screen; when off, it runs silently in the background.
toolsInfo: Choose which tools DSH loads at startup; fewer tools use less context.
indicatorInfo: Shows on screen when DSH uses your mouse and keyboard. Background actions show nothing.
progressInfo: Floating step view; clicking × closes the current window without turning the feature off.
stopInfo: Press Esc to stop DSH using your mouse and keyboard.
previewTitle: Save indicator settings and preview on screen
clearShortcutTitle: Remove the custom stop key and keep Esc only.
browserChange: After saving, browser changes wait for the current action, then close the DSH browser.
toolsChange: After saving, tool selection changes wait for the current action.
shortcutConflict: Lock shortcut cannot match the stop shortcut.
invalidOverlay: Enter valid overlay numbers and a supported lock shortcut (Esc is reserved).
updateRestartDesktop: Restart DSH to use it: right-click the DSH icon in the taskbar tray, choose Quit, then reopen DSH Desktop (closing the window is not enough).
updateRestartWeb: Restart dsh web to use it.
updateSyncing: The new version was just released. Waiting for the plugin market to pick it up, usually a few minutes.
updateBusyWaiting: The plugin market is finishing another install; the update continues after it.
updateAgentsRunning: An agent is running, and the plugin market does not update meanwhile. Choose Retry after it finishes.
updateMarketWaiting: The plugin market has not picked up the new version yet. Try again later.
updateNpmUnavailable: The latest version on npm could not be confirmed. Try again.
updateMismatch: The installed version is not the new one; try again later.
updateFailedHint: Try again later, or update by hand with the command under How to update.
updateDialogRestart: Restart DSH to use it. Restarting stops any task in progress.
updateDialogRefresh: Reload the page to use it.
updateDialogReady: The new version is in use.
updateRestarting: DSH is quitting and will open again shortly.
updateStageCheck: Checking that the plugin's files can be replaced…
updateStopInstallTitle: The plugin market is replacing the plugin's files. Interrupting would break the plugin, so this step cannot be stopped.
updateStopLate: Installing has already begun and can no longer be stopped; it will finish shortly.
updateStopUnsupported: This version of the plugin market cannot stop an update midway, so the update continues.
updateStopped: Update stopped. The plugin is still v{version}.
updateLocked: Another program is using the plugin's folder, so an update would fail and could break the plugin; it was not started. Quit and reopen DSH (this also closes the apps on the hidden desktop), close any File Explorer or terminal window open in that folder, then choose Retry.
updatePluginRemoved: The update did not finish, and the plugin market also removed the plugin from DSH. Quit and reopen DSH, then search the plugin market for dsh-computer-use-win and install it again.
updateMarketFallback: You can also update it in the plugin market, which lists new versions some time after npm, so v{version} may take a while to appear there.
updateOpenMarket: Open Installed in the plugin market
updateMarketManual: The plugin market was not found: update it under Settings → Plugin Market → Installed in DSH.
reportTitle: Save diagnostics to your Downloads folder, then open that folder and GitHub's new-issue page
reportIssueOpened: Opened {issueLink}. Describe what happened and attach this file.
reportAttachFile: Open {issueLink}, describe what happened, and attach this file.
reportFailed: The diagnostics file could not be saved.
reportCancelled: Saving the diagnostics file was cancelled.
reportDescribeIssue: You can still describe what happened on {issueLink}.
reportUnconfirmed: The export could not be confirmed. Check your Downloads folder.
reportBusy: A diagnostics export is already running.
reportOpenIssue: Open a new issue on GitHub
modeQuietHint: Keep using your PC and the task keeps going: DSH works in the background where it can and borrows the mouse and keyboard only briefly.
modeQuietNote1: Apps DSH opens run on a hidden desktop and never pop up in front of you.
modeQuietNote2: Steps that need the mouse and keyboard borrow them briefly, right away: the window flashes forward and back, and your keys and clicks meanwhile are held, then replayed.
modeQuietNote3: DSH waits a moment while you hold a key or button, have input-method text not yet committed, or use a full-screen app.
modeQuietNote4: Quitting DSH closes the apps on the hidden desktop; anything unsaved there is lost.
modeFastHint: For when you step away: DSH keeps its window in front and uses the mouse and keyboard directly, the fastest way. Press Esc to stop.
modeVmHint: Works inside a Hyper-V virtual machine and never touches your PC; it uses the VM’s own files and apps. Set it up once first.
hypervStep1: Turn on Hyper-V: in “Turn Windows features on or off”, select Hyper-V and restart (Windows Home does not have it).
hypervStep2: Let your account manage Hyper-V: open PowerShell as administrator, run the line below, then sign out and back in.
hypervStep3: In Hyper-V Manager, create a Windows 10 or 11 virtual machine and install Node.js 22 or later in it.
hypervStep4: Sign in to the VM’s desktop with your Windows account and stay signed in; you can close the Hyper-V preview window.
hypervStep5: Enter the VM’s name below, exactly as Hyper-V Manager shows it, and choose Save changes.
hypervStep6: Choose Configure connection and enter that account’s user name and password (not a PIN) in the window that opens.
hypervReady: Connection configured. DSH now works in this virtual machine.
hypervMissingNode: Sign-in saved. Step 3 is left: install Node.js 22 or later in the VM, then choose Configure connection again.
hypervMissingDesktop: Sign-in saved. Step 4 is left: sign in to the VM’s desktop with this account, then choose Configure connection again.
hypervFailed: The Hyper-V connection could not be configured.
hypervErrUnavailable: Hyper-V is off on this PC; see step 1.
hypervErrPermission: Your Windows account cannot manage Hyper-V yet; see step 2.
hypervErrVmState: The virtual machine cannot start now; start it in Hyper-V Manager first.
hypervErrVmUnknown: No virtual machine has this name; check the name in step 5.
hypervErrSignIn: Could not sign in to the VM: check that it has reached the desktop and that the user name and password are right (steps 4 and 6).
